headline: Federal Reserve Cuts Rates 25 Basis Points to 4.25% as Inflation Eases
summary: The Federal Open Market Committee cut its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to a target range of 4.00 to 4.25% on Wednesday, marking the third consecutive rate cut as core PCE inflation drifted toward 2.4%. Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell pointed to a softening labor market in his post-meeting press conference.
key_points: FOMC cut rates 25 basis points to a 4.00 to 4.25% target range
Third consecutive rate cut as core PCE inflation reached 2.4%
Unemployment ticked up to 4.3% in the prior month's report
Fed Chair Jerome Powell signaled openness to additional cuts at upcoming meetings

source_documents.title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement on monetary policy
source_documents.quote_text: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace, but job gains have moderated and the unemployment rate has moved up since earlier in the year.
